analyst_view.overall: Early view: José Mourinho's Real Madrid have won eight in a row, including 3-0 at Valencia, and Vinícius has served his domestic ban, but Rodrygo, Raúl Asencio and Ferland Mendy are out and Mourinho has complained about how little rest his internationals get. Celta came into November with the league's best defence (seven conceded in ten games) but have five injured players, including Borja Iglesias. Madrid host PSV on Tuesday and Celta host Bournemouth on Thursday.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Celta under Giráldez are built on clean sheets and draws (six in their first ten games), and Madrid's international players will have little time to recover before kick-off. A 2-0 or 2-1 looks more likely than an open game.

corners.text: The site expects 8.9 corners. Mourinho's Madrid hurt teams in transition rather than through long spells of pressure, and they took only five corners while dominating at Mestalla. Celta prefer to keep the ball rather than sit in their box.

cards.text: The model has 4.0 cards. Celta are a tidy, ball-playing side (eight fouls and one yellow against Levante), and Madrid's three yellows at Valencia came from an unusually heated game. I expect three or four.

shots.text: The site expects 28.0 shots, which fits. Madrid had 19 at Valencia, and Celta still created 23 against Levante, so they will try to have some say even at the Bernabéu.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 on target. Celta's compact block forces opponents into lower-quality shots, and they had the league's best defensive record into late October. Madrid's front line is back to full strength with Vinícius, but I'd still expect about nine.
